questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the usual way to give a short affirmative answer in Chinese?
Name three verbs which may not be repeated as short answers.
Which word do you use to give a short "yes" answer to questions containing these verbs?
Which verb do many speakers not repeat as a short answer?
Give a short affirmative answer in Chinese to Nǐ zhù zai Mínzú Fàndiàn ma?
Why can't zhù be used as a short answer?

answers.answer_text: Because zhù is one of the verbs which may not be repeated as a short answer; shì is used instead.

questions_and_answers.question_text: What are the meanings of xìng and jiào?

answers.answer_text: Xìng means "to be surnamed" and jiào means "to be given-named."

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the full Chinese answer meaning "Yes, I'm staying at the Nationalities Hotel."

answers.answer_text: Shì, wǒ zhù zai Mínzú Fàndiàn.

questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the Chinese name of the Nationalities Hotel?
If a question uses the verb shì, what would the short affirmative answer be?

answers.answer_text: Shì — the verb of the question is simply repeated.

articles.text:
2. B: Nǐ zhù zai Mínzú Fàndiàn ma?         Are you staying at the Nationalities
                                            Hotel?
   A: Shì, wǒ zhù zai Mínzú Fàndiàn.        Yes, I'm staying at the Nationalities
                                            Hotel.

Note on No. 2

Shì: The usual way to give a short affirmative answer is to repeat the verb used in the question. Some verbs, however, may not be repeated as short answers. Zhù is one such verb. Others not to be used are xìng, "to be surnamed," and jiào, "to be given-named." Many speakers do not repeat the verb zài as a short answer. To give a short "yes" answer to questions containing these verbs, you use shì.
